requirement:
A record's `references` digest MUST be rewritten only if the
{term}`requirements.refactor.mapped_back` current reference set of its subject,
under {cite}`requirements.ci.reference_set`, has the recorded digest.
rationale:
I judged this from the supplied test source only. I did not request any implementation source.

**Obligation.** `requirements.refactor.reference_digest` says a record's `references` digest is rewritten only if the mapped-back current reference set of its subject has the recorded digest. That gives two testable outcomes:
- (a) When the mapped-back set matches the recorded digest, the digest is rewritten to the new set's digest. The record must then validate as current.
- (b) When the mapped-back set does not match, nothing is rewritten and the change is reported.

**(a) Match, so rewrite.**
- `tests/refactor.rs#fn[a_moved_function_keeps_its_evidence_current]` authors a record and moves `fn[load]` to another file. The reference's file and selector change, so the digest must be recomputed from the mapped-back set to match. The test shows the record is stale before the refactor, with an error mentioning `fn[load]`. After the refactor it asserts `errors(root)` is empty, so the rewritten digest is the correct one. It also checks that an unaffected record (`rules.check`) stays byte-identical, and that a second run changes 0 records.
- `tests/refactor.rs#fn[a_moved_file_rewrites_anchors_and_paths]` moves a file named by an `:impl:` anchor. It asserts the anchor is rewritten and that `errors(root)` is empty afterwards. This covers the anchor-based reference-set entry.

**(b) Mismatch, so no rewrite.**
- `tests/refactor.rs#fn[a_reference_set_changed_beyond_the_mapping_blocks_every_rewrite]` renames the definition `rules.load=core.load` and adds an extra `{impl}` that the mapping does not explain. It asserts the report says "the reference set of core.load changed". It asserts the report does not mention a text change, so the text and requirements-input rewrites are blocked too. It asserts the record file is byte-identical.
- `tests/refactor.rs#fn[a_changed_reference_set_is_reported_on_a_record_reading_nothing_moved]` covers a record that reads no moved node, so only its reference set is involved. A node moves and an unmapped `{impl}` is added. It asserts the "reference set of rules.check changed" report and that the file is unchanged.

**Other considerations.**
- The different kinds of change the digest detects are all handled by the digest comparison. They are adding or removing a reference, changing its role, and editing its commentary. They do not need separate tests here. The details of the digest encoding belong to `requirements.ci.reference_set`, which is cited context and not reassessed.
- A moved definition with an unchanged reference set is covered by the positive tests above.

The tests cover both directions of the "only if" condition with assertions on outputs and on file contents. I found no gap.

text: :::{req} reference_digest
A record's `references` digest MUST be rewritten only if the
{term}`requirements.refactor.mapped_back` current reference set of its subject,
under {cite}`requirements.ci.reference_set`, has the recorded digest.
:::{req} reference_set

A definition's reference set MUST consist of its current incoming `{impl}`, `{test}`, and `{fixme}` edges, except a `{fixme}` inside a site of the definition under {cite}`requirements.references.site_review`, under {cite}`requirements.references.roles` and
{cite}`requirements.references.anchors`: for each edge, its role and the file and
outline selector of the node the reference belongs to under
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`, or of the anchored file or
node, and, for a fenced reference in a source outside the book, the words of
its body under the word rule of {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`.
`{cite}` references MUST NOT contribute. The reference-set digest MUST be
the SHA-256 digest of an unambiguous encoding of those entries in sorted order,
so it does not depend on line numbers or on the order references are found.
For a structural assessment under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.structural_review`, the digest MUST additionally
include a versioned structural-assessment marker. A record predating structural
assessment MUST therefore be stale, including a legacy record with a wildcard
review version. Other assessments MUST retain their existing digest encoding.
Authoring MUST record the digest of the reference set it supplied, and
validation MUST recompute it and report a changed reference set as stale
evidence. Adding or removing an `{impl}`, `{test}`, or `{fixme}` reference or anchor,
changing its role, editing its commentary, or moving it to a different node
MUST therefore make the evidence stale even when no recorded input changed; moving a reference within
the node it belongs to MUST NOT.
:::{definition} mapped_back
:phrase: mapped-back
The *mapped-back* form of current text or a current address is the text or
address with each new side of the mappings replaced by its old side.
